inputs.original_text: South Dakota Governor Larry Rhoden signed a bill on Thursday that requires new registered voters to prove that they are United States citizens in order to cast a ballot in state elections. In the press release, Senate Bill 175 was explained to: only appl[y] to state elections and only impacts new registrants. inputs.modified_text: Calling Senate Bill 175 a “limited safeguard” doesn’t make it harmless. Restricting new registrants in state elections still puts another barrier between people and the ballot, while “confidence” rhetoric can make exclusion sound like responsible governance. Voting should be accessible, and any state rule that narrows who gets to participate deserves serious scrutiny—not a presumption that it protects democracy.
